claims.text: SELF-FAMILIARITY evaluates a large language model's familiarity with concepts in an input instruction prior to response generation.
SELF-FAMILIARITY withholds response generation when concepts in the input instruction are identified as unfamiliar.

evidence.description: The authors introduce SELF-FAMILIARITY as a pre-detection self-evaluation technique focusing on evaluating concept familiarity in input instructions.
The approach withholds generation of response in case of unfamiliar concepts, emulating the human ability to refrain from responding.

methodologies.name: SELF-FAMILIARITY
methodologies.description: A pre-detection self-evaluation technique that assesses model familiarity with input instruction concepts and withholds response generation for unfamiliar topics.
conditions: evaluated across four different large language models

limitations.text: Existing hallucination detection techniques rely on intricate CoT or parameter-based methods that suffer from interpretability issues.
Post-generation hallucination detection methods cannot prevent hallucinations from occurring and suffer from inconsistent performance due to instruction format and model style.
